Corporate.tagline: Managed security services and SOC operations for mid-market enterprises.
Corporate.brandDescription: Tunbridge Cybersecurity Holdings operates a portfolio of managed security service brands across SOC, MDR, vCISO, and compliance consulting.
Corporate.scope:
Tunbridge operates across:
• 24/7 SOC and MDR services
• vCISO engagements for mid-market enterprises
• Compliance and audit-readiness consulting (SOC 2, ISO 27001, HIPAA, PCI)
• Incident response retainer programs
• Multi-brand operations under a unified ticketing and SOC platform
Corporate.mission: To provide enterprise-grade managed security operations to mid-market customers under a single multi-brand operator.
Corporate.vision: A managed security operator whose mid-market customers receive the same quality of SOC service Fortune 500 customers expect from the global firms.
coreValues: Senior — partners are accountable on every engagement.
Operational — the SOC runs around the clock.
Reliable — the same SLA this Tuesday and next.
Discreet — customer relationships and incidents stay private.
Corporate.brandNameRationale: Tunbridge is a real English town name (Royal Tunbridge Wells in Kent), used here in the holding-company convention of named-place + category + Holdings (Compass Diversified, Constellation Software, Vista Outdoor). The single-place + Cybersecurity + Holdings format reads as an institutional operator with a regional headquarters and multi-brand portfolio.
Corporate.manifesto: Tunbridge Cybersecurity Holdings owns and operates a portfolio of managed security service brands. Each brand retains its identity, customer base, and SOC analysts; we operate the shared platform, threat intelligence, on-call rotation, and back-office. The buyer is an MSSP founder considering sale, a mid-market enterprise consolidating vendor relationships, or an institutional investor holding security-services assets.
Corporate.industrySummary: Managed security services has consolidated under a small number of global firms (Secureworks, Trustwave, BAE Applied Intelligence) and the cloud-platform vendors (Microsoft Defender, AWS Security Hub). The opening underneath is for a serious mid-tier multi-brand operator with deep SOC operations and the procurement reliability mid-market enterprise customers require.
Corporate.competitorLandscape: Arctic Wolf (arcticwolf.com) is the modern MDR reference. Secureworks (secureworks.com) holds the legacy MSSP peer slot. eSentire (esentire.com) sits in the MDR mid-market middle. Expel (expel.com) plays in the modern transparent-SOC position. We belong in the regional mid-tier multi-brand MSSP category.
Corporate.positioningStatement: Tunbridge Cybersecurity Holdings is a regional multi-brand managed security operator running SOC, MDR, vCISO, and compliance services for mid-market enterprises.
Corporate.positioningRationale: We compete on SOC operations depth, threat-intelligence breadth across the portfolio, and the procurement-grade reliability mid-market enterprises require for multi-year managed-security relationships.

Creative.tagline: A security firm that publishes everything.
Creative.brandNameRationale: Changelog is the published list of changes in software — a real engineering and operations trade word. The definite article + Co suffix follows the considered-creative trade-name school.
Creative.manifesto: Most cybersecurity brands sell fear. The breach, the threat, the nation-state actor. We made Patch Notes because the actual work of security is mostly fixing things, one at a time, in a long quiet list. We sell the fix. We sell the changelog. We are not a fear brand. We are a maintenance brand.
Creative.industrySummary: Cybersecurity branding has been polished, fear-based, and slightly cold. There's room for a brand that's warm, character-driven, sticker-friendly, and serious about the actual maintenance work that keeps systems secure.
Creative.competitorLandscape: Tailscale (tailscale.com) does warm-technical security well. 1Password (1password.com) holds the design-led consumer position. Cloudflare (cloudflare.com) does the infrastructure peer. We sit warmer and more honest about the work than any of them.
Creative.positioningStatement: A security brand for the people doing the maintenance.

targetAudience.primary: 25 to 45. Security engineers, DevOps engineers, IT operations managers. They already use three security tools and want the fourth to be the one their team actually likes.

dos: Show the patch and what it fixed

Talk like the engineer who'd be implementing the fix

Creative.tagline: A security firm built around what attackers actually try.
Creative.brandDescription: The Honeypot Project is a creative-led security boutique that runs deliberate decoy systems and publishes what it learns from the attacks that land on them.
Creative.scope:
The Honeypot Project works across:
• Deception-engineering and honeypot deployment
• Threat-intelligence research from observed attacks
• Quarterly published reports on attacker behaviour
• Custom honeypot design for enterprise customers
• Open-source tooling for the security research community
Creative.mission: To learn what attackers actually do by letting them try, in places where it doesn't matter.
Creative.vision: A security firm whose quarterly attacker-behaviour report is the most-read research in the industry.
coreValues: Specific — every claim is tied to observed data.
Research-led — the report is the brand.
Direct — published methodology, not closed-source claims.
Slightly wry — security is serious; we don't have to be solemn.
Creative.brandNameRationale: Honeypot is the real cybersecurity trade term for a decoy system deliberately exposed to attract attackers and study their methods. Project frames the brand as ongoing and research-led. The definite article gives the proper-noun register of a research initiative. Stands in the lineage of declarative research-led security brands (Project Zero, The Shadowserver Foundation register).
Creative.manifesto: Most cybersecurity marketing argues by analogy — 'imagine if an attacker tried X'. We started The Honeypot Project to argue from observation. We run honeypots, watch what real attackers actually try, and publish the data. The brand is the research output. The firm sells what the research enables.
Creative.industrySummary: Threat intelligence has matured into a recognized category but most firms produce intelligence from internal telemetry, not from deception-engineering research. There is real space for a creative-led firm whose primary output is published research from deliberately-exposed decoy systems.
Creative.competitorLandscape: GreyNoise (greynoise.io) holds the closest peer slot in deliberate-exposure research. Shadowserver Foundation (shadowserver.org) sits in the foundation-research middle. Recorded Future (recordedfuture.com) plays the threat-intelligence platform reference. Mandiant (mandiant.com) is the elite incident-response peer. We belong alongside GreyNoise with a stronger published-research register.
Creative.positioningStatement: The Honeypot Project is a security firm that runs decoy systems and publishes a quarterly report on what real attackers actually do.
Creative.positioningRationale: The brand competes on the published research. The quarterly Honeypot Report is the marketing artefact and the proof of expertise. Custom engagements are downstream of the research reputation.

targetAudience.primary: CISOs, threat-intelligence analysts, and security researchers at large enterprises and government bodies.
behaviors: Read security research as part of weekly work.
Run internal honeypots or want to.
Care about the methodology behind a finding.
motivations: Want intelligence grounded in observation, not modeling.
Want a firm with a clear research voice.
Want to know how the attackers are actually thinking this quarter.

dos: Publish the quarterly report on a published date.
Show the actual logs in research material.
Name the attacker techniques by their MITRE ATT&CK ID.
Reference observed attempts by date and decoy environment.

messagingPillars.name: The quarterly report
messagingPillars.description: Every quarter we publish the Honeypot Report — observations from our deliberately-exposed decoy environments, with attacker techniques, source patterns, and methodology notes. It's free.

Creative.tagline: A security firm built around deception and forensics.
Creative.brandDescription: Decoy & Trace Co is a creative-led security firm specializing in deception engineering and digital forensics, with engagements that combine deliberate decoys and traceable attack analysis.
Creative.scope:
Decoy & Trace Co works across:
• Deception engineering and honeypot deployment
• Digital forensics for incident reconstruction
• Published quarterly research on attacker behaviour
• Open-source forensics tooling
• Custom decoy deployments for enterprise customers
Creative.mission: To make deception engineering a primary security practice rather than a research curiosity.
Creative.vision: A firm whose decoy environments become standard references for serious attacker research.
coreValues: Specific — every claim is tied to observed data.
Research-led — the research is the brand.
Direct — published methodology.
Literary — the writing about deception is part of the work.
Creative.brandNameRationale: Decoy and Trace are the two foundational deception-engineering trade words — the bait and the analysis. Paired they ground the brand in the specific craft. Co is the small-firm suffix. No 'The' prefix.
Creative.manifesto: Most security firms react after incidents. We started Decoy & Trace Co because the actual most informative security work is deliberate — deploying decoys, observing attempts, tracing attacker behaviour.
Creative.industrySummary: Deception engineering has matured as a research practice but is rare as a primary commercial offering. There is real space for a firm positioned explicitly on decoy-and-trace work.
Creative.competitorLandscape: GreyNoise (greynoise.io) plays the closest peer in deliberate-exposure research. Shadowserver Foundation (shadowserver.org) sits in the research-organization peer position. We belong alongside GreyNoise with a forensics complement.
Creative.positioningStatement: Decoy & Trace Co is a security firm specializing in deception engineering and digital forensics with combined engagements.
Creative.positioningRationale: The brand competes on the decoy-and-trace premise.
